Having lived near Indian Reservations all my life I think I have come to a better understanding or Native American vs European settlers. First of all we have recognize that there were many different Indian Cultures and each culture responded in a different way to the European settlers. The second thing we must understand that that the Native American Culture was on the cusp of a cultural shift. That cultural shift was the changing of the Native American way of life from a hunter-gatherer society to an agrarian way of life. In the hunter-gatherer society there was not a lot of Labor input into the land. There for land had a different meaning to them than it did for the agrarian Native American that put a lot of manual labor and time into the raising of crops. The concept of Land to the Agrarian Native American was a lot closer to the European concept of land. The major difference between the two concepts was that the in the Native American agrarian society land was more communal than individually owned. Even to day most assets of production on the Reservations are Tribal owned and not individually owned. This places most of the political power in the hands of a few people. Now while these people work for the interests of the group as a whole they always seem to live a much better life style than the other members of the tribe. Also this communal ownership of land did not have the same cache as individual ownership in the legal systems that the Europeans brought with them. If the Native American Culture had a affinity for individual ownership of a asset of production I suspect that the Native Americans would have integrated into the European culture with a lot less violence and long standing grievances.

The agrarian Native Americans were a lot more organized than the hunter gatherer Native Americans. The heartland of the agrarian Native Americans was in the upper Mississippi and Ohio River valleys. These tribes that the economic viability to fight the European settlers to a stand still from roughly 1760 to 1830 or 60 years of conflict. The rest of the Native American Cultures were dominated in about 20 years or that period of time from 1860 to 1880. There were some Native American conflicts that Occurred after 1880 Mainly with the Sioux Nations and the Apache of the South west. I find that it is note worthy that the longest and bloodies fight with the Native American population was with an Agrarian culture but the last Native American wars was with Hunter-gatherer populations.
